context: A 3x2 grid of linked scatterplots showing 7 health metrics (height, weight, age, resting HR, systolic BP, cholesterol, VO2 max) across 300 synthetic individuals in 3 activity groups (Active, Moderate, Sedentary). Panels support brush-based selection with union/intersection toggle and staged annotations (count badge, centroid crosshair, outlier flags).
first_impression: Clean and well-organized — six panels with a restrained 3-color palette feel immediately readable without overwhelming the viewer.
what_works: The 3-color Tol palette (blue/pink/green) separates the three activity groups distinctly across all panels without ambiguity; the 3x2 grid with consistent cell sizing and shared visual encoding makes cross-panel comparison natural rather than effortful.
what_doesnt: Point density in some panels (especially Cholesterol vs Systolic BP) produces visible overplotting that obscures within-group distributions even at r=3.5 with 0.65 opacity; the staged annotation system (centroid crosshair at 400ms, outlier flags at 900ms) cannot be evaluated for animation congruence from a static screenshot — whether the progressive reveal aids or distracts from brushing is unknown.
